correctness.rationale: Support classes C_S are false-twin classes of size product(q_i-1), forcing all but one vertex from each class in every resolving set. For each binary coordinate i, the complement-support class C_[n]\{i} has the unique neighbor supported on {i}, forcing one additional selected vertex beyond the twin bound. For n>=3 these charging pairs are disjoint. The explicit construction containing all-but-one from every class plus each binary singleton contains a singleton-support landmark for every coordinate; symmetric-difference coordinates resolve omitted representatives, and a coordinate outside any proper support dominates its omitted representative.

A 2024 paper on dominant metric dimension treats selected rings such as Z_n rather than arbitrary mixed direct products, and a 2026 semisimple-ring paper treats determining and ordinary metric dimensions but not resolving domination.

value.rationale: The 2023 source presents resolving domination for products of finite fields but leaves a clean structural gap between its all-binary and all-nonbinary regimes. The theorem closes that gap for every n>=3 with a uniform formula and identifies the exact algebraic correction: one additional landmark for each F_2 factor. This is a natural complete classification of the mixed family, not a parameter tweak or isolated computation.
